Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Definition of IaaS
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): A cloud service
model that provides infrastructure resources such as
servers, storage, and networks over the Internet.
With IaaS, users can rent hardware resources
instead of having to invest and manage physical
infrastructure.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Basic components of IaaS
➢ Servers: Virtual or physical servers.
➢ Storage: Store data on virtual drives
➢ Networking: Firewall, load balancer, network
management
➢ Virtualization system: Create virtual servers,
optimize resources
➢ Management and Automation: Management and
automation tools
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Types of servers in IaaS solutions
Physical Servers (Máy chủ vật lý)
Dedicated Virtual Servers (Máy chủ ảo
chuyên dụng)
Shared Virtual Servers (Máy chủ ảo dùng
chung)
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Physical Server
✓ Are actual hardware devices, providing
resources such as CPU, RAM, hard drive and
network connection.
✓ Located in data centers and managed by
businesses or cloud service providers.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Physical Server
➢ Hardware
✓ Processor (CPU): Handles computations and processing tasks.
✓ Memory (RAM): Temporary data storage for active processes.
✓ Storage: Hard disk drives (HDD) or solid-state drives (SSD) for storing
data permanently.
✓ Motherboard: Connects all hardware components.
✓ Power Supply: Provides power to the server.
➢ Operating System
✓ A physical server typically runs an operating system (OS) like
Linux or Windows Server. This OS directly interfaces with the
hardware.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Physical Servers
➢ High performance
➢ Comprehensive customization
➢ High load capacity
➢ Characteristics of physical server
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Physical Servers
✓ Advantages of physical servers
▪ High and stable performance
▪ Comprehensive control
✓ Disadvantages of physical servers
▪ High initial investment costs
▪ Difficulty in expansion
▪ Complex management and maintenance
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Physical Servers
➢ Applications suitable for physical servers
✓ Applications suitable for physical servers
▪ High and stable performance
▪ Comprehensive control
✓ Big Data Analytics
▪ High initial investment costs
✓ Critical Enterprise Applications
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Dedicated virtual server
➢ Definitions and basic concepts
❖ These are virtual servers that provide separate
resources, not shared with other servers on the
same physical server.
❖ Provides the same high performance and stability
as physical servers, but with less flexibility and
cost.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Dedicated virtual server
➢ Characteristics of dedicated virtual servers
✓ Stable performance: Provides stable and
reliable performance.
✓ Highly customizable: Customize resource
configuration according to specific needs.
✓ Flexible scalability: Easily expand or reduce
resources.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Dedicated virtual server
➢ Characteristics of dedicated virtual servers
✓ High performance: Separate resources, not
affected by the load of other servers.
✓ Good security: Enhance security, reduce the risk
of attack.
✓ Easy management and customization:
Comprehensive control, simple management tools.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Dedicated virtual server
➢ Disadvantages of dedicated virtual servers
✓ Higher cost compared to shared virtual
server: Higher cost, need to consider.
✓ Management and maintenance requirements:
Requires management and maintenance skills.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Dedicated virtual server
➢ Applications suitable for dedicated virtual servers
✓ Applications requiring high security:
Financial and medical applications.
✓ Large enterprise applications: ERP, CRM
systems.
✓ Web applications and online services: E-
commerce websites, cloud services.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Shared virtual server
➢ Definitions and basic concepts
❖ These are virtual servers that share resources
with other virtual servers on the same physical
server.
❖ Resources such as CPU, RAM, and storage are
divided and shared among multiple users.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Shared virtual server
➢ Characteristics of shared virtual servers
✓ Resource sharing: Use part of the physical
server's resources together with other virtual
servers.
✓ Low cost: Suitable for small businesses,
personal websites or projects with limited
budgets.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Shared virtual server
➢ Advantages of shared virtual servers
✓ Cost savings: Cost is much lower than physical
servers and dedicated virtual servers.
✓ Easy to manage and deploy: Simple
management, easy to deploy and manage
applications.
✓ Flexibility: Easily expand or contract resources
according to needs.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Shared virtual server
➢ Disadvantages of shared virtual servers:
✓ Unstable performance:
✓ Lower security
✓ Limited customization:
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Types of servers in IaaS solutions -Shared virtual server
➢ Applications suitable for shared virtual servers
✓ Personal websites and blogs: Personal websites,
blogs and small projects.
✓ Small and medium enterprises: Small and
medium enterprises with limited budgets.
✓ Test and development projects: Test and
development projects need flexible and low-cost
environments.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Storage
Object Storage: Stores data in the form of
objects.
Block Storage: Provides blocks of data that can be
attached to the server.
File Storage: A shared file system accessed by
multiple servers.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Networking
Virtual Network: Connects servers and
services in the cloud
Firewall: Control traffic and protect security.
Load Balancer: Distributes traffic evenly
between servers.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Virtualization system
Hypervisor: Creates virtual servers from
hardware resources.
Containerization: Virtualization at the
operating system level, packaging applications
in containers.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Components of IaaS - Management and Automation
Management Tools: Resource management
interface and dashboard.
Automation: Tools to automate resource
deployment, management and expansion.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Definition of load balancing
Load Balancing: Is the process of distributing
traffic and processing work evenly between servers
or system resources to ensure that no resource is
overloaded and the system operates smoothly
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Main components of load balancing
Load Balancer: Device or software that
distributes traffic
Backend Servers: Servers handle requests
from users
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ How load balancing works
Traffic distribution: Traffic distribution:
Load balancer distributes requests to backend
servers.
Health monitoring: Check the status and
performance of backend servers.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Popular load balancing algorithms
Round Robin: Distribute requests in
sequential order
Least Connections: Distribute requests to the
server with the fewest connections.
IP Hash: Uses the client's IP address to
identify the server.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Benefits of load balancing - Increase load capacity and system performance
Workload distribution: Prevent overload at a
specific server.
Enhanced processing capabilities: Improve
application responsiveness.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Benefits of load balancing - High availability and reliability
Redundancy and fault tolerance: Redirect
traffic when a server fails
Auto-scaling: Add or remove resources based
on traffic.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Benefits of load balancing - Improve user experience
Reduced response time: Distributes
workload evenly for faster response time.
Increased application performance:
Applications run smoother, minimizing
interruptions.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Benefits of load balancing - Enhanced security
Protection against DDoS attacks: Distribution
of malicious traffic and sudden offloads.
Additional security solutions: Prevent
additional security threats.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Benefits of load balancing - Reduce operating costs
Optimize resource usage: Make the most of each
server's performance, reducing excess resources.
Easier management: Simplify system management
and monitoring.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
Redundancy is the creation of copies or the
establishment of alternative mechanisms to ensure
that systems and data can continue to operate
normally when a failure occurs.
Target: Ensure high availability and reliability for
the system. Minimize downtime and data loss.
➢ Redundancy concept and target
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Types of redundancy
Hardware Redundancy: Server, hard drive,
power source, network connection.
Software Redundancy: Backup copies of
software or services.
Network Redundancy: Redundant network
connection.
Data Redundancy: Back up data in many
different locations.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Data Redundancy methods
Backup: Full, incremental, differential backup.
Disaster Recovery: Recovery plan and process.
Data Replication: Copy data to many different
locations
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Benefits of redundancy - Ensuring service availability and continuity:
High Availability: The service is always available.
Business Continuity: Minimize downtime, maintain
business operations.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Benefits of redundancy - Data protection
Data Loss Prevention: Back up and clone
data to protect it
Disaster Recovery: The process of recovering
systems and data after major incidents.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Benefits of redundancy - Increase system reliability and performance
Downtime Minimization: System inactivity
is minimized.
Performance Enhancement: Balances work
load, increases overall performance.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Benefits of redundancy - Enhanced security
Protection Against Cyber Attacks: Protects
data and systems from cyber attacks.
Access Management and Control: Only
authorized people can access.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Benefits of redundancy - Optimize operating costs
Reduced Incident Response Costs: Reduce
costs associated with troubleshooting and
system recovery.
Resource Optimization: Distributes workload
evenly, reducing unused resources.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Using cloud-based NAS(Network Attached Storage) devices
- NAS is a data storage device connected to a
network, allowing users to access and share data
from any device with a network connection.
- NAS acts as a centralized storage server,
providing storage space and data management
services to many users and devices.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Using cloud-based NAS devices
➢ Benefits of cloud-based NAS
Access data anytime, anywhere: Access from
anywhere with an Internet connection.
Flexible scalability: Easily expand storage
capacity.
High security: Data encryption, access control,
security monitoring.
Easy management: Intuitive management interface,
integrated management and automation tools.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Using cloud-based NAS devices
➢ Examples of cloud NAS providers:
Nirvanix CloudNAS: Object storage, flexible
scalability, easy integration.
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP: High
performance, security, standards compliance.
Google Cloud Filestore:
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Using cloud-based NAS devices
➢ Cloud-based NAS applications
Store and share data: Store documents, images,
videos, share between users and workgroups.
Backup and restore data: Back up important
data, restore when necessary.
Storage for cloud applications: Storage for
databases, data analytics, web services.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
➢ Advantages of IaaS solutions
✓ Reduce initial investment costs:
▪ Save hardware and infrastructure costs.
▪ Pay according to your needs, optimize your budget.
✓ Flexibility and scalability:
▪ Easily expand or contract resources.
▪ Customize resource configuration according to needs.
✓ Save operating and maintenance costs:
▪ Reduce maintenance and management costs.
▪ Automate and manage easily.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
➢ Advantages of IaaS solutions
✓ Enhance security and regulatory compliance:
▪ Multi-layer security: Data encryption, access control,
security monitoring.
▪ Comply with international standards and regulations:
ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA.
✓ Enhance availability and reliability:
▪ Backup system and disaster recovery.
▪ Global data center network.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Common IaaS Use Cases
➢ Data Storage and Backup
✓ Use IaaS to store and back up data, ensuring
safety and quick recovery.
✓ For example: Use Amazon S3 for daily data
storage and backup..
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Common IaaS Use Cases
➢ Development and Testing
✓ Set up development and testing environments on
IaaS, easily create and delete environments.
✓ Example: Using Microsoft Azure to develop and
test software applications.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Common IaaS Use Cases
➢ Website and Application Hosting
✓ Host websites and applications on IaaS,
ensuring high availability and performance.
✓ Example: Use Google Cloud Platform to host an
e-commerce website.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Common IaaS Use Cases
➢ Disaster Recovery
✓ Set up a disaster recovery solution, backing up
data and automated systems.
✓ Example: Use IaaS to back up a financial
institution's systems and data.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ Common IaaS Use Cases
➢ Running High-Performance Applications
✓ Run applications that require high
computational resources such as big data
analysis and artificial intelligence.
✓ Example: Use Amazon EC2 to run complex
machine learning models.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ The role of IaaS in business
✓ Digital conversion support:
▪ IaaS provides flexible and efficient infrastructure,
supporting businesses in their digital transformation.
✓ Cost optimization:
▪ Reduce initial investment costs and operating costs.
▪ Pay as you go, optimize your budget.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ The role of IaaS in business
✓ Increased flexibility and scalability:
▪ Expand or contract resources according to business needs.
▪ Adapt to market fluctuations.
✓ Enhance security and regulatory compliance:
▪ Advanced security measures and compliance with
international security standards.
▪ Protect data and applications from threats.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ The role of IaaS in business ✓ Enhanced performance and availability:
▪ Provide hardware and network resources with high
performance.
▪ Backup and disaster recovery solutions, ensuring
high availability.
✓ Support for application development and
deployment:
▪ Provides flexible development and testing
environments.
▪ Deploy applications quickly and effectively.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
➢ Main IaaS services of AWS - Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)
✓ Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers (instances)
with the ability to customize resource
configurations such as CPU, RAM, and storage.
✓ Users can easily create, manage, and shut down
instances as needed.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
➢ Main IaaS services of AWS - Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service)
✓ Amazon S3 is an object storage service that allows
data to be stored and retrieved at any time from
anywhere.
✓ Supports unlimited data storage and ensures high
sustainability.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
➢ Main IaaS services of AWS - Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud)
✓ Amazon VPC enables the creation of virtual private
networks, providing an isolated and secure network
environment in the AWS cloud.
✓ Users can control entire network configuration such
as IP addresses, subnets, and security settings.
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
➢ Main IaaS services of AWS - AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management)
✓ AWS IAM enables access management and control
of user and service permissions on AWS.
✓ Provides features such as multi-factor
authentication (MFA), role-based access control
(RBAC).
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
➢ Benefits of using AWS IaaS
✓ Flexibility and scalability
✓ High performance and reliability
✓ Security and compliance
✓ Cost optimization
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Microsoft Azure IaaS
➢ Microsoft Azure's main IaaS services
✓ Azure Virtual Machines
✓ Azure Blob Storage
✓ Azure Virtual Network
✓ Azure Active Directory
✓ Azure Site Recovery
✓ Azure Monitor
✓ Azure Backup
✓ Azure Load Balancer
Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
❖ IaaS Providers - Google Compute Engine
➢ Main IaaS services of Google Compute Engine
✓ Google Compute Engine
✓ Google Cloud Storage
✓ Google VPC (Virtual Private Cloud)
✓ Google Cloud IAM (Identity and Access
Management)
THANKS

❖ Improve performance through load balancing
➢ Popular load balancing algorithms
Round Robin: Distribute requests in
sequential order
Least Connections: Distribute requests to the
server with the fewest connections.
IP Hash: Uses the client's IP address to
identify the server.

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:
❖ System redundancy and data storage
Redundancy is the creation of copies or the
establishment of alternative mechanisms to ensure
that systems and data can continue to operate
normally when a failure occurs.
Target: Ensure high availability and reliability for
the system. Minimize downtime and data loss.
➢ Redundancy concept and target

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Types of redundancy
Hardware Redundancy: Server, hard drive,
power source, network connection.
Software Redundancy: Backup copies of
software or services.
Network Redundancy: Redundant network
connection.
Data Redundancy: Back up data in many
different locations.

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:
❖ System redundancy and data storage
➢ Data Redundancy methods
Backup: Full, incremental, differential backup.
Disaster Recovery: Recovery plan and process.
Data Replication: Copy data to many different
locations

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:
❖ Using cloud-based NAS(Network Attached Storage) devices
- NAS is a data storage device connected to a
network, allowing users to access and share data
from any device with a network connection.
- NAS acts as a centralized storage server,
providing storage space and data management
services to many users and devices.

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:

Access data anytime, anywhere: Access from
anywhere with an Internet connection.
Flexible scalability: Easily expand storage
capacity.
High security: Data encryption, access control,
security monitoring.
Easy management: Intuitive management interface,
integrated management and automation tools.

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:

✓ Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers (instances)
with the ability to customize resource
configurations such as CPU, RAM, and storage.
✓ Users can easily create, manage, and shut down
instances as needed.

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:

✓ Amazon S3 is an object storage service that allows
data to be stored and retrieved at any time from
anywhere.
✓ Supports unlimited data storage and ensures high
sustainability.

sections.heading: Part 5: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
sections.text:

✓ Amazon VPC enables the creation of virtual private
networks, providing an isolated and secure network
environment in the AWS cloud.
✓ Users can control entire network configuration such
as IP addresses, subnets, and security settings.

(RBAC).
